newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesia Cilacap visbreaker restarts October 13.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Cilacap visbreaker restarts October 13.

text.p: A 55,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) visbreaker at Indonesia's Cilacap refinery resumed operations on October 13 after start-up delays following a maintenance shutdown at its crude distillation unit (CDU), a refinery source said on Monday.
"The visbreaker is normal since Sunday," the source told Reuters by telephone.
The visbreaker was closed along with a 200,000-bpd crude unit between September 1 and October 7. Three attempts to restart the visbreaker had failed.
The refiner had made a fourth attempt to restart the visbreaker on October 10. But a delay in obtaining spare parts again interrupted plans to start the unit last week, he said.
Low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) is fed into a visbreaker to reduce its viscosity, or to lighten its waxy texture, and to produce naphtha and distillates.

Industry sources in Singapore had said that because of the visbreaker start-up problems, the 200,000-bpd CDU was forced to reduce its crude runs in order to limit its LSWR or fuel oil output. But the refinery source said, since the CDU resumed operations early this month, it has been running at full capacity. The excess LSWR had been put in tankers, he added.

The Cilacap refinery complex, which is located in Central Java, has another CDU with a 100,000-bpd capacity. This unit processes Middle East crudes, while the bigger CDU processes a cocktail of sweet Indonesian crudes such as Ardjuna and Attaka.
